module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Toronto spaces

A *Toronto space* is a topological space
which is homeomorphic to all of its subspaces of same cardinality.

It is conjectured that every T2, Toronto space is discrete.
W.R. Brian proved that this holds under GCH.

*References:*
 - [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toronto_space)
 - [The Toronto problem](https://wrbrian.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2012/01/thetorontoproblem.pdf) by *W.R. Brian*
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Toronto

open Cardinal

variable (X : Type*) [TopologicalSpace X]

/-- A *Toronto space* is a topological space
which is homeomorphic to all of its subspaces of same cardinality.
-/
class TorontoSpace where
  toronto : ∀ ⦃Y : Set X⦄, #Y = #X → Y ≃ₜ X

/-- Every finite space is Toronto, since
the only subspace with same cardinality is the space itself.
-/
@[category test, AMS 54]
instance Finite.torontoSpace [Finite X] : TorontoSpace X where
  toronto := by
    intro Y hY
    have eq : Y = Set.univ := by
      refine (Set.eq_univ_iff_ncard Y).mpr ?_
      have : Y.ncard = (#↑Y).toNat := by
        exact rfl
      rw [this, hY]
      exact rfl
    rw [eq]
    exact Homeomorph.Set.univ X

/-- Any T2, Toronto space is discrete. -/
@[category research open, AMS 54]
theorem DiscreteTopology.of_t2_of_torontoSpace [T2Space X] [TorontoSpace X] :
    DiscreteTopology X := by
  sorry

-- TODO: Add implication that this holds under the GCH

end Toronto

reformulations.difference: The class stores chosen homeomorphisms for all full-cardinality subspaces, including the whole space. Wikipedia phrases the definition as being homeomorphic to every proper full-cardinality subspace.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The whole-space case is supplied by Homeomorph.Set.univ. Homeomorphisms can be inverted, and classical choice selects one for each eligible subspace without imposing any compatibility requirement. In /workspace/review/scratch.lean, I proved Nonempty (TorontoSpace X) ↔ ∀ Y : Set X, Y ≠ Set.univ → #Y = #X → Nonempty (X ≃ₜ Y), without using the conjecture.

reformulations.difference: The discreteness conjecture is stated for every cardinality, whereas Wikipedia singles out uncountable spaces as the unresolved case.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Finite Hausdorff spaces are discrete. Countably infinite Hausdorff Toronto spaces are also discrete, as stated on Wikipedia and in Brian's introduction and Corollary 6.2. Thus universal discreteness is equivalent to discreteness restricted to uncountable Hausdorff Toronto spaces; including the smaller cases adds no unresolved content.

sources_consulted: W. R. Brian, The Toronto problem, especially the Introduction, Proposition 2.6, and Corollary 6.2: https://wrbrian.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2012/01/thetorontoproblem.pdf
review.notes: Checked all three declarations. Cardinal equality and the induced subtype topology have the intended meanings. The finite-space instance is sorry-free, and its use of ncard/toNat is safely restricted by [Finite X]. Lean checks covered empty and singleton spaces, arbitrary finite spaces, finite Hausdorff discreteness, and infinite discrete Toronto spaces. The scratch file compiles without errors or warnings. Brian's Proposition 2.6 confirms the docstring's GCH result for spaces of any size; the general problem remains open in the consulted sources. Toronto.lean matches the specified commit and was not modified.
